case_number: CIVIL APPEAL NO. 1144 OF 2022 (ARISING OUT OF SLP (C) NO. 19059 OF 2019)

parties.respondent: The Chairman and Managing Director TANGEDCO & Ors.

summary: The appellants, aggrieved by a Madras High Court judgment upholding the appointment of ITI Helpers through direct recruitment with a 15% weightage for viva-voce, challenged the introduction of interview after prior notification suggesting no interview. The Supreme Court considered whether the interview, conducted to assess physical fitness for pole climbing and cycling, was arbitrary. Relying on the Justice Khalid Commission report, the Court examined compliance with selection norms, including the 1:1 ratio between existing workers and skilled ITI candidates. The process followed 85% weightage for academic marks and 15% for viva-voce, adhering to government orders and reservation policies.
legal_provisions_cited: G.O.Ms. No. 18, Labour and Employment (N2) Department, dated 25.02.2008
G.O.Ms. No. 65, Personnel and Administrative Reforms (Personnel) Department, dated 27.05.2009
Tamil Nadu Electricity Board, Administrative Branch Memo No. 100459/265/G.57/G.572/2007 dated 03.02.2009
final_judgment: Special leave granted. Appeals allowed with directions to uphold the selection process including viva-voce as valid, non-arbitrary, and in accordance with recruitment guidelines and the Justice Khalid Commission recommendations.
